- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially after sharp spikes or during early parts of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lag in recognizing short-term volatility or policy shocks.
- After a spike in history (e.g., 49.61, 49.30), model fails to correct downward quickly; instead, it overshoots and then slowly reverts — indicating poor handling of mean reversion after peaks.
- Model underestimates sharp downward corrections (e.g., 49.61 → 35.94) and fails to anticipate sudden drops in the second half of the forecast.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes high peaks — model doesn’t sufficiently “reset” after high points.
- Model exhibits poor sensitivity to low-price periods (e.g., 35–38 range) — tends to ignore or underweight them, leading to overconfidence in mid-to-high price zones.
- Horizon-specific: First 5–10 days of forecast are often too high; last 5–10 days are too low — suggesting model lacks dynamic adjustment to recent volatility or policy changes.
- Model doesn’t adequately capture “rebound” or “reversion to mean” after sharp declines — often underestimates the magnitude of recovery.
